# opencode-node

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@matrix2305/opencode-node)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@matrix2305/opencode-node)

A node plugin for OpenCode V2: a local OpenCode server connects to a remote
OpenCode server ("hub") and loads its agents, skills, commands, MCP servers and
file-based memory from there.

Status: **0.2.0** — setup + memory sync, CLI, cache-first startup, TUI
commands, conflict-safe push, tests, build and publish pipeline.

## How it works

```
hub (OpenCode 2.x, /home/matrix2305)
  ├─ /api/agent, /api/skill, /api/command, /api/config
  ├─ /api/fs/list, /api/fs/read
  └─ ~/.config/opencode, ~/agents

node (this machine)
  ├─ ~/.config/opencode-node/config.json     hub URL + passwordRef
  ├─ ~/.local/share/opencode-node/
  │    ├─ snapshot.json                      cached setup + hashes
  │    ├─ skills/<id>/SKILL.md               materialised skills
  │    └─ backup/<timestamp>/...             backups before overwrite
  ├─ ~/.config/opencode/agents/*.md          written from the hub
  ├─ ~/.config/opencode/commands/*.md        written from the hub
  └─ opencode.jsonc                          hub config + node plugin entry
```

On every OpenCode start the plugin applies the cached snapshot immediately
(skills are registered at runtime, agents/commands are files), then refreshes in
the background if the cache is older than `cacheSeconds`.

## Install

From npm:

```bash
npm i -g @matrix2305/opencode-node
oc-node init \
  --hub https://matrix2305.tailbd26da.ts.net \
  --password-ref keychain:opencode-matrix2305
```

With custom sync dirs:

```bash
oc-node init \
  --hub https://hub.example \
  --password-ref keychain:my-hub \
  --root remote=.config/opencode,local=~/.config/opencode,type=setup \
  --root remote=opencode-memory,local=~/opencode-memory,type=memory \
  --root remote=shared-docs,local=~/docs,type=mirror
```

From this repo:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
node dist/cli.js init --hub <url> --password-ref <ref>
```

- `--password-ref` accepts `keychain:<service>`, `secret:<name>`, `file:<path>`,
  `env:<VAR>` or a raw password (not recommended).
- `--config` replaces `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` with the hub config
  (mode 0600, backup kept) and removes the legacy `opencode.json` so only one
  document is active. The node plugin entry is preserved.
- `--restart` runs `opencode service restart`.
- Without `--config`, only agents/skills/commands/MCP are synced; local
  providers/models stay untouched.

## CLI

```bash
oc-node status           # hub, cache age, counts, applied state, config drift
oc-node doctor           # config, password, plugin entry, hub reachability
oc-node pull             # refresh snapshot + materialise files
oc-node push             # push locally changed memory back (conflict-safe)
oc-node pull --config    # also replace local opencode.jsonc with the hub config
oc-node config           # apply the config from the current snapshot
oc-node restart          # opencode service restart
```

The published CLI is `dist/cli.js` (Node >= 22). In the repo you can also run
`node src/cli.ts <command>` (Node 23+).

## Model list

`pull` fetches the hub's model list (`/api/model`) and the server plugin applies
it with a model transform: any local model that the hub does not have is set
`enabled: false`, so the picker shows exactly the hub's models. Disabled models
are not deleted — if the hub re-adds them later, the next refresh re-enables
them.

## Provider credentials (live, no files)

`sync.auth` (default on) pushes the hub's provider credentials **straight into
the local OpenCode server's credential store** during `init`, `pull` and every
background refresh:

- CLI path: `POST /api/integration/<id>/connect/key` on the local server.
- Plugin path: `ctx.integration.connect.key` with a stable label
  (`opencode-node:<hub>`), so re-syncs replace instead of stacking.
- Keys are never written to `auth.json` or any file, never logged, and never
  persisted in the snapshot (only a count + hash of provider names).
- Works without restarting the server — new keys are usable immediately.

## Plugins

`sync.plugins` (default on) pulls the plugin layer from the hub during
`oc-node init` and every `oc-node pull`:

- hub `plugins` / `plugin` entries are appended to the local `plugins` array
  (object form and options preserved, local entries never removed, idempotent);
- `~/.config/opencode/plugin/` and `plugins/` trees are copied;
- `package.json` dependencies are merged (local wins on conflicts).

The server plugin does the same on startup and after each refresh, then emits
`plugins` so the TUI can prompt for a restart. OpenCode installs npm plugins into
`~/.cache/opencode/npm` on the next start or `opencode reload`.

```bash
oc-node pull            # syncs setup, memory and plugins
oc-node pull --config   # also replaces opencode.jsonc with the hub config
```

## Multiple hubs

```bash
oc-node hub list
oc-node hub add work --url https://work.example --password-ref secret:opencode-work
oc-node hub use work --pull
oc-node hub remove work [--purge]
```

Each hub has its own `snapshot.json`, `applied.json` and skill cache under
`~/.local/share/opencode-node/hubs/<name>/`. Local agents, commands, memory and
`opencode.jsonc` are shared; the active hub's pull owns them (with backups).
Legacy single-hub configs migrate automatically.

## Config/providers modes

`sync.config` controls the raw hub `opencode.jsonc` (providers, models, plugins,
MCP):

| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `off` | never touch the local config |
| `manual` | only `oc-node config` / `oc-node pull --config` |
| `auto` | write the hub config when its hash changes |

```bash
oc-node config --mode auto      # set + apply now
oc-node config --mode manual
oc-node config --dry-run
```

Auto apply keeps the node plugin entry, removes the legacy `opencode.json`,
records `applied.config`, backs up every overwritten file, and logs
`config:auto-applied`. Restart OpenCode for a guaranteed clean load.
`auth.json` (provider credentials stored outside config) is not synced.

## What is synced

| Category | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Skills | `ctx.skill.transform` at runtime; `SKILL.md` materialised under the data dir |
| Agents | `~/.config/opencode/agents/<id>.md` + `ctx.agent.reload()` |
| Commands | `~/.config/opencode/commands/<name>.md` + `ctx.command.reload()` |
| MCP | `ctx.mcp.transform` from the hub config |
| Config/providers | raw hub `opencode.jsonc` written locally (0600), plugin entry preserved, `off`/`manual`/`auto` modes |
| Sync dirs | configurable at init (`--root`): setup / memory / mirror types, repeatable |
| Memory | `~/agents/<agent>/` folder mirror with conflict-safe push (no memory tools; the hub memory plugin does that) |
| Plugins | hub `plugins` list merged into the local config, `plugin/` files copied, `package.json` dependencies merged |
| Auth | hub provider credentials connected **live** into the local OpenCode server (`connect/key`); never written to files |
| Models | hub model list applied at runtime; local-only models are disabled (`enabled: false`), nothing deleted |

## TUI

Server slash commands:

- `/node-status` — hub, cache age, counts, memory state.
- `/node-sync` — force a pull.
- `/node-push` — push memory changes.

TUI part (home footer + palette commands, live via RPC):

- footer status: `node 9s · 62m` (skills · memory, `↑` = pending)
- **opencode-node: status** — dialog with hub/cache/counts/memory.
- **opencode-node: sync now** — pull + toast.
- **opencode-node: push memory** — push + conflict/upload toast.
- Startup and `updated` event toasts.

## RPC

The server registers `matrix2305.opencode-node`:

- `status`, `sync`, `push`
- event `updated` (`kind`, `summary`)

```bash
curl -u opencode:<password> -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":{}}' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:49374/api/rpc/matrix2305.opencode-node/status?location[directory]=/home/me'
```

## Memory (folder sync only)

Memory is a **folder mirror**, not a memory implementation. The hub config
installs the memory plugin; that plugin owns search, storage and prompts.

- Hub workspace `~/agents/<agent>/` is mirrored to `~/agents/<agent>/` on the
  node (paths rewritten between `/home/matrix2305/agents` and the local root).
- A locally modified file is never overwritten by a pull; it stays until pushed.
- Push is three-way: hub sha vs local hash vs last synced `localSha`. If both
  sides changed, a `.conflict-<node>-<timestamp>` copy is written and the hub is
  left untouched.
- A 10 s scan (`memory.syncIntervalSeconds`) pushes pending changes;
  `node.sync` and RPC `sync` pull and then push; `oc-node push` and RPC `push`
  are manual.
- No custom memory tools and no prompt injection. The only tools this plugin
  exposes are `status` and `sync`.

## Runtime constraints found in 2.3.0

- `AgentEditor` has no `add`; agents must be files + reload (asynchronous).
- `Skill.Info.path` must point to an existing file.
- Do not pass optional fields as `undefined` (`autoinvoke: undefined` silently
  drops the skill).
- `Command.Info` has no template; command files are copied instead.
- `/api/config` contains provider keys; never log it.
- `/api/fs/*` resolves relative paths against `location[directory]`; the client
  always sends the configured remote root.
- MCP transforms apply immediately, but `ctx.mcp.list()` is empty until the
  server connects.

See `docs/M0-FINDINGS.md` for the spike report.

## Security

- `config.json`, `opencode.jsonc` and the password file are `0600`.
- Secrets are never logged. Prefer `keychain:`/`secret:` over a password file.
- The hub password gives full filesystem access to the hub; treat it as a
  server admin credential.
- Every overwritten file is backed up under
  `~/.local/share/opencode-node/backup/<timestamp>/`.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
node dist/cli.js status
```

Build: tsup → `dist/index.js` (server), `dist/tui.js` (terminal),
`dist/cli.js` (CLI). See `docs/PUBLISH.md` and `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`.

Repo layout:

```
src/config.ts    config file, password refs, paths
src/hub.ts       OpenCode hub client (Basic auth)
src/sync.ts      pull, snapshot, materialise, config apply
src/index.ts     OpenCode V2 plugin (cache-first + refresh + node tools)
src/cli.ts       oc-node CLI
docs/            findings and design notes
```

# Compatibility

## OpenCode

| Component | Range | Tested |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local server / plugin API | `@opencode/plugin` 2.x | 2.3.0 |
| Hub server | OpenCode 2.x (`/api/*`) | 2.3.0 |

OpenCode 1.x is not supported: its plugin API and server API differ. The plugin
checks the hub with `GET /api/info` and refuses to pull when the major version
is not `2`.

The package declares `peerDependencies: { "@opencode/plugin": ">=2.0 <3" }`.
OpenCode loads its own copy at runtime; the plugin never bundles it.

## Hub endpoints used

| Endpoint | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/info` | version + reachability |
| `GET /api/agent` | agents (with `location[directory]`) |
| `GET /api/skill` | skills |
| `GET /api/command` | command names (templates come from files) |
| `GET /api/config` | MCP servers |
| `GET /api/fs/list` | workspace files (memory) |
| `GET /api/fs/read/*` | memory, command and config files |
| `POST /api/experimental/fs/write` | memory push |

`/api/fs/*` calls send `location[directory]` set to `paths.remoteRoot`, so
relative paths resolve against the configured root instead of the server's
default location.

## Node runtime

- CLI (`dist/cli.js`): Node >= 22.
- Plugin (`dist/index.js`): runs inside OpenCode's Bun/Node runtime; no extra
  native dependencies.
- TUI part (`dist/tui.js`): loads only in the terminal client; no JSX/OpenTUI
  peer dependencies in 0.1.0.

## Known API constraints

- `AgentEditor` has no `add`; agents are files + `ctx.agent.reload()`.
- `Skill.Info.path` must point to an existing file.
- Optional fields passed as `undefined` silently drop a skill.
- `Command.Info` has no template; command files are copied.
- `/api/config` may contain provider API keys; never log it.
- MCP transforms apply immediately; `ctx.mcp.list()` is empty until connected.
- Plugin tool definitions require a server restart after upgrading the package
  in place.

## Tested combinations

- macOS 26 (arm64), OpenCode 2.3.0, Node 26, hub OpenCode 2.3.0 on Linux.
- Linux (headless) hub via Tailscale HTTPS with a valid certificate.

# M0 findings — runtime capabilities of `@opencode/plugin` 2.3.0

Validated against a live OpenCode 2.3.0 hub (`matrix2305`) inside an isolated
server (temp `HOME`/XDG dirs, custom port).

## Works

| Feature | API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load plugin from local dir | `plugins: ["/path/to/dir"]` | dir with `index.ts` is enough |
| Network from `setup` | `fetch` | Basic auth against hub works |
| Skills | `ctx.skill.transform(editor.add)` | `path` must point to a real file; content is served from cache |
| Commands | `ctx.command.transform(editor.add)` | `Command.Info` from hub has no template |
| Commands (files) | write + `ctx.command.reload()` | new command visible after reload |
| Agents | write markdown + `ctx.agent.reload()` | not immediate in `ctx.agent.list()`; visible on the API shortly after |
| MCP | `ctx.mcp.transform(editor.set)` | registered server appears on `/api/mcp`; `ctx.mcp.list()` may be empty until connected |
| Location loading | `GET /api/location?location[directory]=...` | must be called before `/api/agent` on a fresh location |

## Gotchas

1. **`AgentEditor` has no `add`.** Runtime agent registration is impossible; use
   files + `reload()`. Agents are eventually visible, not synchronously.
2. **`Skill.Info.path` must exist.** Passing a path to a not-yet-written file
   silently drops the skill.
3. **Optional fields must be omitted, not `undefined`.** `autoinvoke: undefined`
   makes `editor.add` silently fail and can poison the transform list.
4. **`Command.Info` has no template.** Sync command files via `/api/fs` and
   `ctx.command.reload()`.
5. **`/api/config` includes secrets.** The config document contains provider API
   keys. Do not log it; if config sync is enabled, write it with `0600` and redact
   logs.
6. **`/api/agent` needs an active location.** On a fresh server, call
   `/api/location` first; otherwise the list is empty.
7. **MCP registration is asynchronous.** The transform returns before the server
   connects; `/api/mcp` shows status `failed`/`connected` separately.

## Next steps (M1)

- `HubClient` with capability probe (`/api/info`), auth, timeouts, retries.
- Config file `~/.config/opencode-node/config.json` + Keychain secret ref.
- CLI `oc-node init|status|pull|doctor`.
- Move spike code into `src/{config,hub,sync}/`.
- Cache-first startup: read snapshot synchronously, register transforms before
  any `await`, refresh in the background.
- Memory: pull agent workspaces, inject via prompt/context hooks, push changes
  with hash-based conflict detection.
- Config/providers: decide between runtime `ctx.provider.transform` and writing
  `opencode.jsonc` + restart. M0 shows transforms are viable for MCP; providers
  need the `Provider.Info`/`Model.Info` mapping.
- Plugins: cannot be registered at runtime; write config + restart.

# M1 — config, CLI, cache-first

## Delivered

- `~/.config/opencode-node/config.json` with `passwordRef`
  (`keychain:`, `secret:`, `file:`, `env:`).
- `~/.local/share/opencode-node/snapshot.json` — cached setup + hashes.
- `~/.local/share/opencode-node/applied.json` — what the local server last applied.
- CLI: `init`, `pull`, `status`, `doctor`, `config`, `restart`.
- Cache-first plugin: applies the snapshot synchronously, refreshes in background.
- Full pull: 9 skills, 3 agents, 2 commands, 1 MCP, raw hub `opencode.jsonc`.
- Config apply preserves the node plugin entry and removes the legacy
  `opencode.json` so only one config document is active.
- Backups before every overwrite.

## Verified

Isolated server (temp HOME/XDG) with a real hub:

```
agents:   build, general, explore, compaction, title, summary, plan,
          genesis2, lawyer-ai, muzej_jugoslavije
skills:   opencode, report, claude-code-plugin, api-tester, dep-audit,
          docker-helper, env-guard, git-changelog-gen, git-commit-guard,
          git-stats, pr-review, superpowers, browser
commands: init, review, goal, claude-code-doctor, btw, mobile, quick
mcp:      zai-web-search (connected)
```

`oc-node status` and `oc-node doctor` pass; `pull` is idempotent.

## Known limits

- First start after config sync can be slow because the hub config enables
  third-party plugins that OpenCode installs on startup.
- `auth.json` (provider credentials stored outside config) is **not** synced.
  Providers configured inline in `opencode.jsonc` are.
- Plugins themselves cannot be registered at runtime; they come from config and
  need a restart.
- Memory is not implemented yet.
- Session state and `opencode.db` are intentionally never synced.

## Next

- M2: memory workspace pull, prompt/context injection, hash-based push with
  conflict files.
- M3: TUI status/commands, publish pipeline (`dist` build, npm scope
  `@matrix2305`), compatibility matrix.

# M10 — provider credentials sync

## Problem

`applyConfig` copies provider definitions from the hub `opencode.jsonc`, but the
API keys saved by `opencode auth login` live in `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`,
which was never synced. A synced provider therefore appeared in the model list
with no usable key.

## Delivered

`sync.auth` (default on):

- `pull` reads the hub's `.local/share/opencode/auth.json` through `/api/fs/read`
  into `snapshot.auth` (`entries` + `sha`); credentials are never logged.
- `applyAuth(snapshot)` merges hub entries into the local `auth.json`:
  - hub wins for providers it defines (that is the point of config sync);
  - local-only providers are untouched;
  - idempotent — matching entries are skipped;
  - backup before write, atomic rename, mode `0600`.
- Applied by `oc-node init`, `oc-node pull`, and prints the merged provider list.
- `oc-node status` shows how many credentials the hub provides.

## Verified

Real hub (`matrix2305`):

```
auth:     2 provider credential(s) on the hub
auth:     1 credential(s) merged (opencode-go) · restart to use them
local auth.json: opencode-go key updated, 15 local providers intact, mode 0600
```

Unit tests: merge keeps local-only, idempotency, creates the file when missing
(19 total).

## Notes

- `zai-coding-plan` already matched locally, so only `opencode-go` merged.
- Push of credentials node → hub is intentionally **not** implemented; the hub
  is the source of truth for keys.
- Restart OpenCode after a merge for the providers to become usable.

# M11 — credentials live in the server, not in files

## Why

M10 wrote hub keys into `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`. Two problems showed
up in practice:

1. The running server ignores that file until a restart — the user still hit
   "API key has expired" because the server kept the old in-memory credential.
2. Duplicating key material into another file widens the surface for leaks.

## Delivered

- `src/auth.ts`:
  - `fetchAuth(hub)` reads the hub's `auth.json` over `/api/fs/read` (memory
    only, never logged).
  - `applyAuthMemory()` connects each provider credential with a stable label
    `opencode-node:<hub>`; optional `list`/`remove` hooks replace old
    hub-labelled credentials instead of stacking.
  - `applyAuthViaLocalServer()` CLI variant using the local server's HTTP API
    (`/api/integration/<id>/connect/key`, `/api/credential`).
- Server plugin (`src/server.ts`): `applyAuthLive()` runs after the cache load
  and after every background refresh via `ctx.integration.connect.key`.
- CLI: `init` and `pull` connect credentials live; `status` prints the hub
  credential count.
- Snapshot no longer stores key material — only `authCount` and a hash of
  provider names (`hashes.auth`).
- `applyAuth` (file merge) removed; tests rewritten for the memory flow (19/19).

## Verified on the live server

```
oc-node pull
auth:     2 provider credential(s) on the hub (applied to the local server, not stored in files)
auth:     2 connected (opencode-go, zai-coding-plan)

opencode run -m opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash → ok-live / final-ok
```

Also verified with `auth.json` emptied (backup kept): the model still works,
proving nothing depends on the file anymore.

## Notes

- The expired OpenCode Console credential from earlier sessions remains removed
  (`auth logout`); stale in-memory credentials of disabled providers disappear
  on the next server restart.
- Node → hub credential push is intentionally not implemented: the hub is the
  source of truth.

# M12 — model list parity with the hub

## Why

After config sync, the local server still listed models from old local
providers (neuralwatt, moonshot-era, deepseek direct, openrouter …), so the
model picker showed entries that could not be used and diverged from the hub.

## Delivered

- `pull` now reads `GET /api/model` from the hub (with location) into
  `snapshot.models` (`providerID`, `id`, `ref`, optional name/hidden/enabled).
  The snapshot hash `hashes.models` covers the reference list.
- The server plugin applies the hub list at runtime with `ctx.model.transform`:
  every local model whose `provider/model` reference is not in the hub list is
  set `enabled: false` (disabled, not deleted — a later hub change can re-enable
  it). Runs after the cache load and after every background refresh.
- `oc-node pull`/`status` print the hub model count; RPC/TUI `status` shows
  `models` in counts; the TUI dialog notes that local-only models are disabled.

## Verified (live)

```

opencode models → 69 entries
diff <(local models) <(hub /api/model) → empty (identical lists)
neuralwatt/* → absent from the picker
opencode run -m opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash → model-ok
```

## Notes

- Disabled models remain in the registry (`enabled: false`); nothing is deleted,
  and `oc-node restore` is unaffected.
- If the hub later adds a model back, the next refresh re-enables it (the
  transform only disables models missing from the hub list).
- Custom local models defined in the local config are also disabled by design;

# M2 — file-based memory

## Delivered

- Hub workspace pull: `~/agents/<agent>/` (62 files on the real hub), excluding
  `.git`, `skills`, `.clawhub`, `.dreams`, `node_modules`.
- Path rewrite on materialise and push:
  `/home/matrix2305/agents` ⇄ `~/agents`.
- Three-way materialise: a local file modified after the last pull is kept, never
  overwritten; hub changes apply only when the local copy is unchanged.
- `context` + `compaction` hooks inject a `<opencode-node-memory>` block for the
  session's agent (SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, AGENTS, MEMORY, project memory, today's
  daily file), capped at `memory.maxInjectBytes`.
- Tools: `memory_search`, `memory_get`, `memory_store`, `memory_push`.
- Conflict-safe push:
  - upload only files whose local hash differs from `localSha`;
  - fetch the remote file first; if it changed since the pull, write
    `.conflict-<node>-<timestamp>` locally and do not overwrite the hub;
  - no deletion propagation.
- Background push timer (`memory.pushIntervalSeconds`, default 300s).
- CLI `oc-node push`, `status` shows memory files and pending changes.

## Verified

- Keyword search only (no embeddings); vector memory is a separate backend.
- Memory is injected only for agents that have a matching `~/agents/<id>`

- Deletions are not propagated from node to hub.

# M5 — config/providers sync modes

## Delivered

`sync.config` now understands three modes:

| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `false` (`off`) | never touch the local config |
| `"manual"` | only `oc-node config` / `oc-node pull --config` |
| `"auto"` | the plugin writes the hub `opencode.jsonc` when its hash changes |

Legacy boolean `true` is normalized to `"manual"` for safety; `false` stays
`false`. Default for new configs is `"manual"`.

CLI:

```bash
oc-node config --mode auto      # set + apply now
oc-node config --mode manual    # apply only on demand
oc-node config --mode off       # disable
oc-node config --dry-run        # show target + hub hash
oc-node config                  # apply the current snapshot
oc-node status                  # shows config mode + drift
oc-node doctor                  # includes config mode
```

Auto apply runs:

- 1.5 s after setup when a cached snapshot exists (so setup is not blocked),
- after every successful background/forced refresh when `config` hash changed.

Each apply:

- writes the hub config to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (mode 0600),
- keeps the node plugin entry,
- removes the legacy `opencode.json` (backup kept),
- records `applied.config`,
- logs `config:auto-applied` and emits RPC `updated` with `kind: "config"`.

## Verified

Temp node, `sync.config = "auto"`, local config containing only the plugin entry:

```
before: { "plugins": ["/Users/.../opencode-node"] }
after:  hub opencode.jsonc (model claude-code/claude-opus-5-5, agents, plugins, mcp)
plugin entry preserved at line 67
opencode.json removed
applied.config = edf93a4c…
log: config:auto-applied {"restartRequired":true}
agents: build … genesis2, lawyer-ai, muzej-jugoslavije
```

## Notes

- Config is applied for the next server start; depending on the host, OpenCode
  may hot-reload the file immediately. A restart (`oc-node restart`) guarantees a
  clean load.
- Provider credentials stored in `auth.json` are **not** synced. Providers whose
  keys are inline in `opencode.jsonc` are.
- Every apply keeps a timestamped backup; `oc-node restore` rolls back.
- Auto mode can change models/providers mid-session if the host hot-reloads the
  config. Use `manual` if that is not desired.

# M8 — memory is folder sync only

## Decision

The hub already installs a memory plugin through config sync. This node plugin
must not duplicate its semantics (search, storage, prompt injection). It only
keeps the memory folders in sync.

## Removed

- `context` and `compaction` memory injection hooks.
- Tools: `memory_search`, `memory_get`, `memory_store`, `memory_push`.
- `memory.maxInjectBytes`, `memory.pushIntervalSeconds`.
- `buildMemoryBlock`, `searchMemory`, `storeMemory` from `src/memory.ts` and
  their tests.

## Kept / added

- Bidirectional folder mirror of `~/agents/<agent>/` with path rewriting.
- Three-way materialise (local edits win, remote applies only when local is
  unchanged).
- Conflict-safe push: `.conflict-<node>-<timestamp>` when both sides changed.
- Automatic scan/push every `memory.syncIntervalSeconds` (default 10 s),
  skipping the push when nothing is pending.
- `node.sync` tool and RPC `sync` now pull **and** push pending memory.
- RPC `push` and `oc-node push` remain for manual sync.
- Status/TUI still show memory file count and pending changes.

## Why

The memory plugin from the hub config (`opencode-mem` or any replacement) is
installed by `sync.config` and provides its own tools. Keeping a second memory
implementation caused duplicate tools and prompt bloat.

## Verified

- `npm test` 13/13 after removing the memory-semantic tests.
- `tsc` clean; build clean.
- Pending detection test: a locally edited file is reported until pushed.

## Notes

- The active hub owns `~/agents`; switching hubs with `oc-node hub use` should
  be followed by `oc-node pull` so the folder reflects the new hub.
- Config sync (`oc-node config --mode auto` / `oc-node pull --config`) is what
  installs the hub's memory plugin on this node.

# M9 — plugins are pulled during install

## Delivered

`sync.plugins` (default `true`) makes the plugin layer part of the pull:

- **Plugin list** — read from the hub config (`plugins` and legacy `plugin`
  arrays in every config document). Values are kept verbatim, including the
  object form `{ "package": "...", "options": { ... } }`.
- **Local plugin files** — `~/.config/opencode/plugin/` and `plugins/` trees are
  copied (nested directories included, `node_modules`/`.git` skipped).
- **`package.json`** — the hub file is merged with the local one; dependencies
  are unioned, local wins on conflicts, other local fields are preserved.
- **Merge semantics** — hub entries are appended to the local `plugins` array.
  Local entries are never removed. Merging is idempotent and works on
  commented JSONC without rewriting the file.

Applied by:

- `oc-node init` (right after the first pull),
- `oc-node pull`,
- the server plugin on startup (cache-first) and after every background refresh
  (emits RPC `plugins`, TUI toast "plugins synced · restart OpenCode").

## Verified

Temp node + temp hub:

```
hub config:  ["hub-plugin-a", {"package":"hub-plugin-b","options":{"k":1}}]
hub files:   plugin/local-one.ts, plugin/nested/two.ts
hub pkg:     dependencies { "@opencode-ai/plugin": "2.3.0", "hub-dep": "1.0.0" }
local config:["my-local-plugin"], pkg { local-only-dep }
```

After `oc-node pull`:

```
plugins:  2 entries, 2 local file(s)
plugins:  2 from hub, 3 file(s) written, config updated
local plugins: my-local-plugin + hub-plugin-a + hub-plugin-b (object form)
files:        plugin/local-one.ts, plugin/nested/two.ts
pkg deps:     @opencode-ai/plugin (local 1.17.11 kept), hub-dep, local-only-dep
```

Second pull: `0 file(s) written` — idempotent.

Real hub: 5 plugin entries pulled (`@khalilgharbaoui/opencode-claude-code-plugin`,
`@bd7pil/opencode-deep-memory`, `opencode-auto-resume`,
`@mohak34/opencode-notifier`, `@joe-broadhead/opencode-history`). After
`opencode reload` all five were installed into `~/.cache/opencode/npm` and loaded:

```
loading plugin id=@bd7pil/opencode-deep-memory
loading plugin id=@joe-broadhead/opencode-history
loading plugin id=@khalilgharbaoui/opencode-claude-code-plugin
loading plugin id=@mohak34/opencode-notifier
```

## Notes

- The hub's `plugins` list is authoritative only for *additions*. Removing a
  plugin from the hub does not remove it locally; delete it from the local
  config, or use `oc-node restore` for a full rollback.
- Plugin code changes only take effect after OpenCode installs and loads them

- `sync.plugins = false` keeps the old behavior (no plugin merge, no plugin file
  copy).
- Skills from the hub plugin (`claude-code-plugin`, `history-recall`) appear
